requirement_statement: The portal SHALL be horse-first and SHALL NOT require an individual owner to create an unnecessary Facility or Organization.
Every portal read or action SHALL evaluate identity, account, tenant, facility, horse, relationship, purpose, time, restriction, and permission at action time.
A portal projection SHALL identify its authoritative source, version or as-of time, provenance, staleness, and applicable correction route.
The portal SHALL NOT silently mutate source-owned horse, care, medical, training, schedule, relationship, agreement, or financial records.
Consolidated multi-facility views SHALL preserve tenant and facility isolation and SHALL NOT pool private communications or records.
Account, invoice, payment, email, emergency-contact, invitation, device, or horse-name match SHALL NOT independently create ownership, guardianship, or portal authority.
The portal SHALL expose owner-visible categories only through explicit source-domain projection contracts and field-level permissions.
Internal staff notes, safeguarding content, private employment data, internal disputes, unrelated facility operations, and other customers data SHALL remain excluded unless specifically authorized.
Communications SHALL be classified using the approved taxonomy before routing, preference application, retention, escalation, and evidence rules are selected.

Ordinary message, owner update, announcement, actionable request, reminder, transaction confirmation, formal notice, emergency alert, safeguarding-restricted, billing, and security communications SHALL remain distinguishable.
The initial channel plan SHALL support in-app, email, push, and optional SMS through replaceable adapters.
Generated, queued, provider-accepted, delivered where evidenced, failed, opened where lawful, acknowledged, and action-completed states SHALL NOT be conflated.
The system SHALL expose delivery uncertainty and channel failure without claiming success unsupported by provider or recipient evidence.
Retries SHALL use stable idempotency and deduplication controls so a provider or queue replay does not create misleading duplicate communications.
Mandatory communications SHALL override only the specific preference or quiet-hours rules authorized for their classification.
Users SHALL be able to understand why a communication was sent, which channel was used, whether action is required, and how to challenge or obtain help.
The system SHALL support controlled owner-to-facility messaging, replies, service requests, clarification, document exchange, and escalation.
The initial product SHALL NOT provide public posting, anonymous messaging, unrestricted member discovery, or cross-facility owner messaging.
A facility broadcast SHALL hide ordinary recipient contact information and SHALL NOT automatically make recipients visible to one another.
Audience evaluation SHALL use current governed relationships and SHALL preserve a versioned issue-time audience snapshot without becoming relationship truth.
Critical notices SHALL use explicit acknowledgment or required action when receipt matters and SHALL NOT rely solely on inferred opens.
Acknowledgment SHALL NOT be treated as consent, contractual assent, agreement acceptance, factual admission, task completion, or payment authorization.
Emergency alerts SHALL support authorized multi-channel routing, alternate contacts, visible escalation, delivery failures, and direct fallback instructions.
Emergency communications SHALL NOT promise dispatch, veterinary response, staff monitoring, or response time unless a separately approved and operationally supported service level applies.
Minor communications SHALL apply the adopted age bands, guardian authority, consent, safeguarding controls, and protected communication routes.
The system SHALL prohibit disappearing messages and hidden adult-minor conversation paths designed to bypass guardians or safeguarding controls.
Guardian visibility SHALL be purpose-specific and SHALL support protected handling where disclosure to a guardian may be unsafe or legally restricted.
A minor reaching a new age band or majority SHALL trigger controlled re-evaluation without erasing historical guardian or assent evidence.
Draft communications may be edited, but material sent communications SHALL preserve author, version, timestamps, corrections, and recipient-visible lineage as applicable.
Formal notices, approvals, acknowledgments, emergency alerts, and consequential communications SHALL NOT be destructively overwritten.
User-facing removal SHALL NOT falsely represent external copies, downloaded files, evidence holds, recipient records, or retained legal records as erased.
Retention and disposition SHALL be selected by communication category, purpose, participant, claims, safeguarding, financial, privacy, and legal-hold rules.
Attachments and media SHALL be validated for type, size, malware, sensitivity, metadata, consent, destination, and independent access permission.
Revoking an attachment link SHALL stop future authorized access where technically possible but SHALL NOT claim deletion of lawfully downloaded copies.
Quiet hours SHALL defer eligible noncritical delivery and SHALL preserve visible classification, timing, and override evidence.
Facilities SHALL NOT relabel routine content as emergency or mandatory solely to bypass user preferences.
Machine-assisted translation SHALL preserve the original, label the translation, identify the controlling language, and expose uncertainty or review requirements.
Consequential translations involving agreements, medical instructions, payment terms, emergencies, or safeguarding SHALL require heightened human review before reliance.
Material portal and communication workflows SHALL support keyboard operation, assistive technology, readable contrast, plain language, non-color status cues, and accessible attachments.
AI may assist with drafts, summaries, translation, categorization, and suggested replies only through approved registered use cases with source and uncertainty controls.
AI SHALL NOT autonomously send formal notices, emergency or medical instructions, dispute outcomes, disciplinary conclusions, financial adjustments, or protected minor communications.
A human author SHALL approve consequential AI-assisted communication, and the final sent record SHALL distinguish the approving actor from the AI assistance record.
AI and analytics SHALL NOT train across tenants on identifiable communication content or infer protected traits, legal guilt, medical condition, or relationship authority.
Service requests SHALL display category, status, responsible domain, next action, correction route, and truthful response expectations.
Submitting or labeling a request urgent SHALL NOT create an unsupported guarantee of acceptance, completion, monitoring, or emergency response.
Source-domain actions arising from a request SHALL be completed and audited in the owning domain, with the portal displaying a bounded status projection.
Relationship-effective termination SHALL end current portal and community access and trigger revocation of active sessions, tokens, caches, and queued sends as applicable.
Former parties may retain only historically authorized communications, agreements, invoices, receipts, shared records, and claims evidence permitted by governing retention and access rules.
Historical retention SHALL NOT create access to new updates, current location, successor-facility information, current staff conversations, or new community discovery.
Support access SHALL be purpose-limited, role-controlled, time-bounded where feasible, attributable, auditable, and visibly identified as support mode.
Support SHALL NOT sign, consent, acknowledge, author, or communicate as the customer, nor conceal the real operator in a customer-attributed record.
Support and moderation tools SHALL enforce the same tenant, facility, horse, record, purpose, safeguarding, and sensitivity boundaries as customer channels, plus any stricter platform controls.
Owner community messaging SHALL remain disabled unless the facility affirmatively enables it and an authorized operational owner and moderation route are assigned.
Community discovery SHALL be limited to verified current owners within the same active barn or facility and SHALL reveal only a minimum community profile.
The system SHALL revalidate both participants current same-facility eligibility, account state, facility enablement, blocks, restrictions, and safeguarding controls before each owner-to-owner send.
Community messaging SHALL use in-app identities and SHALL NOT expose private phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses, billing data, horse medical data, or other sensitive details by default.
A block SHALL promptly prevent new peer contact through the bounded community feature while preserving the blocked users ability to report safety concerns and preserving required evidence.
A report SHALL open a reason-coded moderation or safeguarding route without automatically determining guilt, liability, discipline, or legal status.

Authorized moderators may apply temporary protective restrictions before final review when necessary, but every action SHALL be attributable, explainable, reviewable, and appealable where appropriate.
Facility and EquineSync kill switches SHALL stop new discovery and sending without deleting historical evidence, reports, or retained communications.
A shared facility, email domain, horse professional, billing relationship, prior membership, or geographic proximity SHALL NOT establish community eligibility.
Cross-facility, public, anonymous, unrestricted, former-owner, or unverified owner messaging SHALL fail closed without disclosing hidden membership or relationship information.
Offline clients may cache only approved bounded content and SHALL visibly distinguish current, stale, unavailable, and revoked states.
Offline composition SHALL create a draft or pending send only; reconnect SHALL require authentication, fresh authorization, relationship and community revalidation, and duplicate protection.
Revocation, blocking, facility disablement, safeguarding restrictions, and relationship termination SHALL win over offline queued peer or facility messages before send.
Search, autocomplete, notifications, analytics, exports, APIs, background jobs, and support tools SHALL apply the same communication and community authorization rules as the primary interface.
Operational telemetry SHALL measure routing, failures, retries, latency, acknowledgment, moderation queues, revocation propagation, and support actions without logging prohibited content or secrets.

The capability SHALL provide administrative tools for delivery diagnostics, moderation, restrictions, corrections, exports, evidence holds, feature disablement, and incident response before enrollment.

Every material action SHALL create an attributable audit event with actor, principal, facility, horse or conversation context, action, reason, outcome, time, source version, and correlation reference as applicable.
Migration or seed data SHALL NOT infer ownership, guardianship, community eligibility, delivery success, acknowledgment, consent, or notice effectiveness from ambiguous legacy fields.
Deployment SHALL use environment separation, least-privilege secrets, feature flags, staged cohorts, monitoring, stop conditions, rollback, and post-release reconciliation.

No implementation, production, provider activation, community activation, or first-user enrollment may be claimed until the applicable PIA gates, evidence, review, and explicit Founder authority are satisfied.

Community activation SHALL require a current facility enablement decision, published rules, assigned qualified moderators, escalation coverage, trained support, tested block and report flows, and rehearsed facility and platform kill switches.
Owner community participation SHALL be voluntary, separately explained, reversible, and SHALL NOT be a condition for boarding, training, lessons, billing, emergency, or core portal access.

Community discovery SHALL return only eligible participating owners through bounded non-enumerable queries and SHALL NOT expose a downloadable roster, private contact data, precise location, billing data, medical data, or horse association by default.

An owner opt-out or block SHALL prevent new peer discovery and contact for that user, and a facility SHALL NOT override the user control for owner-to-owner communication. Mandatory facility notices remain a separate facility-to-owner channel.

Owner-to-owner community messaging SHALL be presented as non-emergency and not continuously monitored; the interface SHALL provide direct routes for urgent horse welfare, safeguarding, facility, veterinary, or emergency concerns.

Facility moderators and platform support SHALL NOT browse private peer content by default. Content access SHALL require a report, safety case, legal obligation, or appeal; least privilege; reason code; conflict check; time limit; visible case state where safe; and complete audit.

Community reports SHALL protect reporter information as required, prohibit retaliation, separate allegation from finding, support temporary protective controls, and provide review or appeal where appropriate.

Community messaging SHALL enforce rate limits, spam controls, harassment controls, block-bypass detection, alternate-account review, and evidence-preserving restrictions without automated guilt or discipline.

Community participation by minors SHALL follow the approved age and guardian model: no direct account under eight; no peer community messaging for ages eight through twelve; and ages thirteen through seventeen disabled by default unless a separately approved protected configuration, guardian linkage, and safeguarding controls apply.

Owner-created group conversations, public feeds, unrestricted community rooms, and cross-facility groups SHALL remain unavailable in the initial scope. Facility broadcasts SHALL NOT be represented as peer group chats.

Facility split, merger, tenancy change, horse move, ownership change, or parent-organization change SHALL trigger fresh eligibility evaluation and SHALL NOT automatically carry community access or conversations across facility boundaries.

Peer message content, community profiles, reports, and participation data SHALL NOT be used for advertising, data brokerage, public profiles, engagement ranking, or cross-tenant identifiable model training.
